en: Theragāthā 4.10 Catukkanipāta,
Paṭhamavagga [The verse is not provided in the source text.]
The Verses of the Elder Dhammika:
“Indeed, the Dhamma protects the one who lives by the Dhamma;
the Dhamma well-practiced brings happiness.”
This is the benefit when the Dhamma is well-practiced:
one who lives according to the Dhamma does not go to a state of misery.
For the Dhamma and the non-Dhamma are not the same.
Both have an equal ripening:
unrighteousness leads to hell,
while righteousness leads to a happy destination.
Therefore, one should indeed apply zeal toward the teachings,
rejoicing thus in the Sugata who is such-like;
the disciples of the excellent Sugata are established in the Dhamma.
The wise are led to go toward the supreme refuge.
The root of the boil has been torn out;
the net of craving has been uprooted.
“Thus, with saṃsāra exhausted, there is nothing left,
like the moon on the full-moon night when it is bright with its rays.
… [said] the Elder Dhammika.
